unclustered.title: It's fair to say we now have "a country of geniuses in a datacenter"
unclustered.summary: OpenAI recently announced their solution to the Navier-Stokes problem and stated "The groups (of agents) varied in size, and the group that produced the Navier–Stokes resolution involved on the order of 10,000 concurrent agents." We can infer (from total compute spend) how many concurrent agents exist in OpenAI at once. One secondary estimate puts the Navier-Stokes bill at ~$15M.Greg Brockman testified under oath that OpenAI expect to spend $50 billion on compute in 2026. This is ~$137M/day. Assuming OpenAI's margins are ~40% for API revenue, (thus $9M cost over 4 days) this puts daily spend at 2.3M/day, or 1.7% of overall daily compute.Since OpenAI stated the 88-hour agent run used 130B tokens, we divide this by 10^4 agents running for 88 hours, and get 150,000tok/agent/hour. (41tps). The number of concurrent agents OpenAI can run at a time is, where f is the fraction of compute dedicated to internal research agents, and lowercase c is the internal cost per token. unclustered.title: OpenAI President on Doing Business in the Wake of Hugging Face
unclustered.summary: According to OpenAI President Greg Brockman, the models that escaped their sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face's servers had yet to go through alignment training. That they were able to break free of the testing environment was not a surprise to OpenAI, but what has happened since has forced them to rethink some things. Today, we talk to Brockman about what OpenAI has learned since the hacking incident and we discuss why he thinks the conversation around model development has to change. We also talk about how OpenAI collaborates and communicates with competitors like Anthropic, how he thinks models should be evaluating what counts as “good writing,” and, of course, we get his thoughts on how seriously we should be worried about the AI doomsday scenarios. (Source: Bloomberg)
unclustered.headline: OPENAI REVEALS: Escaped Models Weren't Safety-Trained
